Human: Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Tank battle game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies.

Medium-size target from MetaProjectDev (an approximate architecture target, not permission to violate the protocol):
- about 9 repository files
- about 46 functions or methods
- about 727 lines of code

File-count quality gate:
- the complete Task list MUST contain between 8 and 10 files inclusive
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files in that total
- combine closely related small types instead of exceeding this budget

Required domain behavior:
- tank movement and orientation
- bounded arena and obstacles
- projectile creation and movement
- projectile collision and damage
- score or winner state
- deterministic tick and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

The architecture separates pure domain logic (headers/implementations) from runtime to keep tests deterministic and fast. Planned file list (total 9 files to satisfy the 8–10 file gate): 1) CMakeLists.txt. 2) src/Main.cpp. 3) include/Geometry.h. 4) src/Geometry.cpp. 5) include/Entities.h. 6) src/Entities.cpp. 7) include/Game.h. 8) src/Game.cpp. 9) tests/test_main.cpp. Concrete implementation tasks by file: - CMakeLists.txt: Define a C++17 project; build a library target for core (geometry/entities/game), an executable for src/Main.cpp linking core, and a test target; enable CTest; set warning flags; no external dependencies. - include/Geometry.h / src/Geometry.cpp: Define integer grid types (Point, Size), Direction enum (N/E/S/W) with rotation helpers, Rect checks, and utility functions: inBounds, advance(Point,Direction), manhattanDistance, intersects/contains. Keep algorithms pure and exception-safe; validate inputs. - include/Entities.h / src/Entities.cpp: Define structs/classes for Obstacle (immutable cells), Tank (id, position, orientation, health, alive flag), Projectile (owner id, position, direction, alive flag), Arena (width, height, obstacle set, occupancy queries). Implement methods: Tank::rotateLeft/rotateRight, Tank::tryMoveForward(Arena), Tank::canFire(Arena), Arena::isBlocked, Arena::addObstacle, Arena::clear, Projectile::step, collision checks with tanks/obstacles/bounds. - include/Game.h / src/Game.cpp: Define GameState (tanks, projectiles, arena, scores, tick counter, winner), Command type (per-tank: None, Move, RotateLeft, RotateRight, Fire), and public API: Game(width,height), reset(default layout), queueCommand(tankId, Command), tick() deterministic order (apply commands then move projectiles then resolve collisions), getScores, getWinner, getTank, getProjectiles, isOver. Validate inputs (invalid tankId or impossible actions ignored safely). Ensure no randomness and no IO in core. - src/Main.cpp: Provide a minimal scripted demo: create game with a small arena and a couple of obstacles, place two tanks at opposite sides, queue a short sequence of commands across a few ticks, run ticks, print a concise summary or exit silently with success. No loops waiting for input; exit deterministically. - tests/test_main.cpp: Include headers only; build a few deterministic scenarios: (1) movement blocked by obstacle, (2) projectile hits and reduces health, (3) winner declared when health reaches zero, (4) reset restores initial conditions. The test also exercises runtime wiring by constructing a Game, queueing commands, calling tick, and asserting state. Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Tank battle game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies.

Medium-size target from MetaProjectDev (an approximate architecture target, not permission to violate the protocol):
- about 9 repository files
- about 46 functions or methods
- about 727 lines of code

File-count quality gate:
- the complete Task list MUST contain between 8 and 10 files inclusive
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files in that total
- combine closely related small types instead of exceeding this budget

Required domain behavior:
- tank movement and orientation
- bounded arena and obstacles
- projectile creation and movement
- projectile collision and damage
- score or winner state
- deterministic tick and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

projectiles leaving bounds are removed","Obstacle blocking: Obstacles occupy fixed grid cells; tanks and projectiles cannot pass through","Firing and projectile motion: Firing spawns a projectile in front of the tank if the spawn cell is free; projectile advances one cell per tick","Collision and damage: Projectile hitting a tank reduces health; projectile is removed upon first collision","Scoring and winner: When a tank’s health reaches zero, the opponent’s score increments; a winner state is set","Deterministic tick order: Within a tick, apply tank commands (move/rotate/fire), then move projectiles, then resolve collisions, ensuring deterministic outcomes","Reset and validation: Reset returns to initial positions, health, scores; invalid commands are ignored safely without side effects"],"Product Goals":["Deliver a clean, testable core domain implementing the tank battle rules deterministically","Keep the architecture small (8–10 files) yet expressive, with clear interfaces and minimal coupling","Provide a minimal non-interactive runtime demo and a reliable automated test path"],"User Stories":["As a player, I want the tank to face a direction and move forward without passing through walls or obstacles","As a player, I want to fire projectiles that travel straight and damage the opposing tank on hit","As a player, I want the game to track score and declare a winner when a tank is destroyed","As a developer/tester, I want deterministic ticks so I can script sequences and assert expected outcomes","As an operator, I want to reset the game to a known state for repeated runs"],"Competitive Analysis":["Classic console-grid tank games (e.g., Battle City-like mechanics) for deterministic grid-based combat","Minimalist command-driven turn/tick-based simulations used in katas for predictable testing","Academic grid-world environments (e.g., simple RL grids) emphasizing deterministic transitions","Headless game logic libraries that separate simulation from rendering for clean testability"],"Competitive Quadrant Chart":"quadrantChart

Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Tank battle game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies.

Medium-size target from MetaProjectDev (an approximate architecture target, not permission to violate the protocol):
- about 9 repository files
- about 46 functions or methods
- about 727 lines of code

File-count quality gate:
- the complete Task list MUST contain between 8 and 10 files inclusive
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files in that total
- combine closely related small types instead of exceeding this budget

Required domain behavior:
- tank movement and orientation
- bounded arena and obstacles
- projectile creation and movement
- projectile collision and damage
- score or winner state
- deterministic tick and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Tank battle game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies.

Medium-size target from MetaProjectDev (an approximate architecture target, not permission to violate the protocol):
- about 9 repository files
- about 46 functions or methods
- about 727 lines of code

File-count quality gate:
- the complete Task list MUST contain between 8 and 10 files inclusive
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files in that total
- combine closely related small types instead of exceeding this budget

Required domain behavior:
- tank movement and orientation
- bounded arena and obstacles
- projectile creation and movement
- projectile collision and damage
- score or winner state
- deterministic tick and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

idea:
Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Tank battle game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies.

Medium-size target from MetaProjectDev (an approximate architecture target, not permission to violate the protocol):
- about 9 repository files
- about 46 functions or methods
- about 727 lines of code

File-count quality gate:
- the complete Task list MUST contain between 8 and 10 files inclusive
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files in that total
- combine closely related small types instead of exceeding this budget

Required domain behavior:
- tank movement and orientation
- bounded arena and obstacles
- projectile creation and movement
- projectile collision and damage
- score or winner state
- deterministic tick and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents
